summary: GitHub pollers key event operations by their complete canonical observation, preventing concurrent observers from conflicting while preserving event-level deduplication

replay.detail: No replay or history rewrite. Graph event listings and idle queue-exit reads fold existing and new observations by event subject.

schema.detail: The github.event v1 subject and fields, including observer, at, head_sha and detail, are unchanged. No tables or generic claim request hashes change.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: New producers use github-event-observation:v1 plus a fingerprint of the subject and all canonical fields instead of github-event:SUBJECT. Exact retries retain their operation; distinct observations do not collide. Old global-key claims remain readable and fold together with new claims as one event. Subscription and watch delivery identities are unchanged. Two unmodified old producers may still conflict with each other; this change does not repair their historical operation conflicts.

downtime.detail: No coordinated shutdown or migration is required.

manual.detail: No manual step for adopting observation keys; pre-existing operation conflicts still require the separate recovery path.

recovery.detail: Older builds can read the unchanged claim fields. Rolling back a producer restores its old global-key collision risk; rolling back graph listing and idle readers also restores their per-observation listing and timestamp behavior.
